data.narrative:
1872 is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $15M to date, founded by SpaceX veterans including Dan Summers (Raptor engine fabrication lead) and Brian Mongilio. The target sector encompasses 10 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable, though a sufficiently robust peer median cannot be established given the lack of same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with comparable profiles.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable methodology. Using the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $38M. This method reflects the observed capital intensity and risk profile of hardware-focused companies at this stage.

Peer-median triangulation was not executable; while 10 same-sector robotics peers exist, the narrow filter (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) yielded insufficient data points to warrant reliance on a median comparable. Applying an all-sector robotics median would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity given variation in business model maturity and capital requirements across the peer set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M, with a median of $38M. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transaction data at this stage and the company's pre-revenue status. Management pedigree from SpaceX provides technical credibility but does not independently resolve execution risk in a capital-intensive sector.
